newsitem.title: CHILE: Codelco, Enami to seek private mining link-ups.
newsitem.headline: Codelco, Enami to seek private mining link-ups.

text.p: Chilean state companies Codelco and Enami will both seek investment deals with private mining firms in 1997 and beyond, Mining Minister Benjamin Teplizky said.
Both companies hope to follow the example of successful joint ventures already signed between Codelco, the world's largest copper mining company, and private mining firms, Teplizky said.

"Codelco and Enami are going to work fundamentally in the direction of raising their capacity, modernizing their plants, and developing projects via associations with third parties -- that is to say, the incorporation of the private sector in these activities," he told a news conference.
"We really hope the good success until now in this area will be the tonic for working in the medium and long term at Codelco," he said.

Codelco's joint ventures have included the El Abra copper mine with Cyprus Amax Minerals, the Agua de la Falda gold project with Homestake Mining and an investment deal with Australian pension fund AMP.
He and Enami vice president Claudio Agostini denied there was any plans for outright privatization of any part of Enami, a state copper refining company, or Codelco.
"This is an issue that's discussed in the press, not in the government," said Agostini, referring to privatization.
But neither he nor Teplizky clarified what the difference was between privatization and "association with private parties."

Codelco has explored prospects for a joint venture, possibly with Chilean pension funds, for its San Antonio copper deposit and Enami has done the same for its Paipote smelter, officials of both companies have said publicly in the past.
Teplizky, outlining plans for Chile's mining sector into the next century, said copper production in Chile would rise to 3.4 million tonnes this year and 4.7 million in 2000 from 3.1 million in 1996.
A series of new projects will start factoring in their production into Chile's total copper output this year, he said.
"We expect 1997 to be a year of transition. Due to the great quantity of projects opened last year, 1997 will a phase for development of projects," he said.

Prospects for gold were also strong, he said. Output was expected to rise to 56,400 kilos this year from 52,090 kilos in 1996, meaning Chile would again become one of the world's 10 largest gold producers as it was "a couple of centuries ago," said Teplizky.
